q: Where was God before the world?
little: God has always been. He had no beginning. Before anything was made, God was already there, full of love.
big: God has no beginning and no end. He was never made. Before the world began there was only God, and he made everything out of love. We cannot picture that, because we live in time and God does not.
more: Children may ask "but where was he?" The honest answer is that "before" belongs to time, and God made time. It is fine to say, "That is a mystery, and a wonderful one."
avoid: Please do not make up a place or a picture, such as "he was up in space".

scripture.label: Psalm 90:2
scripture.quote: Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.

little: God is not a body like ours, so our eyes cannot see him. But he can see you, and he is always near. One day, in heaven, we will see him.
big: God is spirit. He does not have a body that eyes can see, so he is not hiding from us. We know him by his gifts, by Jesus, and by prayer. The Church teaches that in heaven we will see God face to face.
more: Some children feel left out because they cannot see God. Remind them that Jesus is how God let us see him: "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father." You can also point to the beauty of the world as a sign.
avoid: Avoid "you will see him when you are good enough". Seeing God is a gift, not a prize.

scripture.label: 1 John 3:2
scripture.quote: but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is

little: Nobody made God. God was never made. He has always been, and he made everything else.
big: Everything that is made has a maker. But God is not something made. God just IS, and he is the one who made everything else. When God told Moses his name, it meant something like "I am". He is the one who always is.
more: This is a very common question, and a good one. You do not have to have a perfect answer. You can say, "Even grown-ups find this hard to picture. We believe God has no beginning."
avoid: Do not say "do not ask that". The question is welcome.

scripture.label: Revelation 1:8
scripture.quote: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,”says the Lord God, “who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.”

q: Where is God? Is he everywhere?
little: God is with you right now. He is not far away. You cannot get away from his love, even in the dark.
big: God made everything, and he is close to everything he made. He is not stuck in one place like we are. The Church teaches that God is present to every creature. That is why you can pray anywhere: in bed, on the bus, or in the garden.
more: A follow-up might be "then why go to church?" Answer: God is everywhere, and we also come together to worship as his family, because Jesus asked us to.
avoid: Avoid "God is watching you" in a scary way. Say "God is with you" instead.

scripture.label: Psalm 139:7-8
scripture.quote: Where could I go from your Spirit? Or where could I flee from your presence? If I ascend up into heaven, you are there. If I make my bed in Sheol, behold, you are there!

q: Does God hear me when I whisper?
little: Yes. God hears every word, even a whisper. He hears a thought too. You never need to shout.
big: Yes. God is close, and he listens to every prayer, loud or quiet. Jesus told us to pray to our Father "who is in secret". A whisper, a few words, or no words at all are all good prayers.
more: Some children think God only hears "proper" prayers. Tell them there is no wrong way to start. "Hello, God" is a real prayer.
avoid: Avoid promising that God will always give what we ask. Say instead that he always hears and always loves us.

scripture.label: Matthew 6:6
scripture.quote: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

little: God does not have a body, so he does not look like anything we can see. But Jesus is God’s Son, and Jesus showed us what God is like: kind and loving.
big: God is spirit, so he has no face or body like ours. Pictures of God are only pictures to help us think. The best way to see what God is like is to look at Jesus, who is both God and a real man who walked on earth.
more: If a child has drawn God as an old man with a beard, that is fine. You can say gently, "That is a nice picture. But God is really bigger than any picture."
avoid: Avoid saying God "is" an old man in the sky.

scripture.label: John 4:24
scripture.quote: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

q: Is God a man or a woman?
little: God is not a man or a woman. God is more than both. Jesus taught us to call God "Father" because he loves us and takes care of us.
big: God is spirit, so God is not male or female the way people are. Jesus taught us to say "Our Father", and the Bible also shows God’s love as a mother’s comfort. The Church teaches that being a good father or a good mother both show a little of how good God is.
more: This is a good moment to say that Father is how Jesus himself spoke to God. We follow his words.
avoid: Do not say that God "is" a man, or that fathers are more like God than mothers.

scripture.label: Isaiah 66:13
scripture.quote: As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.”

little: Yes. God loves every single person he made, all around the world. That includes you, and it includes people who are not nice to you.
big: Yes. The Bible says "God is love". God made every person and loves every person, including those who are far from him. He wants everyone to know him and be happy with him.
more: A child may ask, "Even bad people?" Yes. God hates the harm they do, but he still loves them and wants them to turn back to him.
avoid: Do not say "God only loves good children".

scripture.label: 1 John 4:8
scripture.quote: God is love

little: God made you because he wanted you. He loves you and wanted you to be here, and to be happy with him.
big: God did not need to make us. He made us out of love, and he made us to know him and love him. Each person is wanted and special. Nobody is an accident to God.
more: Children who feel unwanted, for any reason, especially need to hear this. It is a sentence worth repeating: "God wanted you."
avoid: Avoid "to be good" as the only answer. Goodness comes after being loved, not before.

scripture.label: Psalm 139:14
scripture.quote: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.

little: God can do anything that is good. He is stronger than anything. But he never does anything that goes against love.
big: God is almighty. Nothing is too hard for him. But God’s power is always joined to his goodness and wisdom. He does not do things that are against his own nature. For example, he cannot lie.
more: Children may ask about silly cases, like "can God make a rock too heavy to lift?" You can smile and say that is a puzzle about words, not about God.
avoid: Avoid giving the idea that God uses his power to scare people.

scripture.label: Luke 1:37
scripture.quote: For nothing spoken by God is impossible.”

little: God is one God, and God is three Persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. It is a great mystery. When we make the Sign of the Cross, we say their names.
big: We believe in one God in three Persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. They are not three gods. The Trinity is a mystery: we cannot understand it all, but we can know it is true because Jesus told us. The Trinity is like a family of love.
more: Pictures like the shamrock or water, ice and steam do not really work, and the Church does not use them as teaching. It is better to say, "It is a mystery. We know God is love, and love is shared."
avoid: Do not say that the Father, Son and Spirit are "three jobs" of one person, or that they are three gods.

scripture.label: Matthew 28:19
scripture.quote: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

q: Does God know everything I do?
little: Yes, God knows you better than anyone, and he loves you very much. He is not looking for mistakes. He is looking after you.
big: God knows every thing about you, even the thoughts nobody hears. The Bible says even the hairs on your head are counted. This is good news. It means you are never alone, and you never have to pretend with God.
more: Some children hear "God sees everything" as being watched by a judge. Turn it around: "God sees everything, and he sees how hard you try."
avoid: Do not use "God is watching" to make a child behave.

scripture.label: Luke 12:7
scripture.quote: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

little: Yes. God made everything, and he thought it was good. Scientists can tell us how and when dinosaurs lived. The Bible tells us that God is behind it all.
big: The Church teaches that God made everything that exists. Scientists study how the world grew and changed over a very long time. The Church says faith and true science never really disagree, because the same God is the author of both. Genesis is not a science book; it tells us who made the world and why.
more: If your child hears that "the Bible says the world is 6,000 years old", be calm. The Catholic Church does not teach that. Catholics are free to learn what science finds.
avoid: Do not make a child choose between God and science.

scripture.label: Genesis 1:31
scripture.quote: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.

little: Because God loves us and takes care of us like the best kind of dad. Jesus called God "Father", and he taught us to do the same.
big: Jesus called God "Abba", which is like saying "Dad". He taught us to pray "Our Father". God is Father because he made us and loves us, and he never leaves us.
more: If a child’s own father is absent or hurtful, "Father" can be hard to hear. You can add, "God is a Father who is always good. He is better than any person can be."
avoid: Do not say "God is like your daddy" if that might hurt.

scripture.label: Matthew 6:9
scripture.quote: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.

q: Why did Jesus have to die?
little: Jesus died because he loves us so much. He gave his life to bring us back to God. And then God raised him up to new life!
big: People sometimes did wrong, and wrong breaks things between us and God. Jesus loved us so much that he gave his whole life to mend that. He did it freely, out of love. Then God raised him from the dead, and death does not have the last word.
more: The Church does not say God was angry and wanted someone punished. The Church says the Father sent the Son out of love, and Jesus freely gave himself. Even the Catechism says this is a mystery we cannot fully explain.
avoid: Do not say "Jesus died because you were bad". Say "Jesus died because he loves you."

scripture.label: John 3:16
scripture.quote: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

scripture.label: Romans 5:8
scripture.quote: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

mystery: The Church does not claim to explain all of it. It is a mystery of love.

little: Yes! Jesus was a baby, then a little boy, then a young man. He grew up in a family with Mary and Joseph. He played, learned, and helped at home.
big: Yes. Jesus really grew up. He learned to walk and talk, he obeyed his parents, and he worked in Joseph’s home. The Bible says he grew in wisdom and in size. We do not know many stories about his childhood, but we know he had an ordinary home life.
more: Children love to imagine Jesus as a child. Stories from outside the Bible about boy-Jesus doing magic are not Church teaching. Keep to what the Gospels say.
avoid: Avoid making up details as if they were from the Bible.

scripture.label: Luke 2:52
scripture.quote: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

q: Did Jesus ever get sad or scared?
little: Yes. Jesus cried when his friend died. He knows what it feels like to be sad. He understands you.
big: Yes. Jesus was truly human, so he had real feelings. The Bible tells us he wept when his friend Lazarus died, and he was in deep distress the night before he died. That means you can bring your sad and scared feelings to him.
more: This can be a gentle way to talk about feelings. "Jesus has felt that too" is true and comforting.
avoid: Do not say that good Christians should never feel sad.

scripture.label: John 11:35
scripture.quote: Jesus wept.

little: Yes. Jesus is God’s Son and he is God. He is also a real person who lived on earth. Jesus is God and man.
big: Yes. The Church teaches that Jesus is truly God and truly man, one Person. The Bible says "the Word became flesh and lived among us". God came close to us by becoming one of us.
more: The Church does not say Jesus is "part" God and "part" man. He is fully both. This is a mystery, and also the heart of Christmas.
avoid: Avoid saying that Jesus is "like" God or "God’s helper".

scripture.label: John 1:14
scripture.quote: The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

little: Jesus is alive! He is in heaven with God the Father. He is also with us, because he promised to be with us always.
big: After he rose from the dead, Jesus went up to heaven. He is alive with the Father, and he has not left us. He is with us in prayer, in the Bible, in the Church, and in the Eucharist. Jesus said "I am with you always".
more: Children often take "went up" literally. You can say heaven is not a place up in the sky, but being with God.
avoid: Do not say Jesus is "far away".

scripture.label: Matthew 28:20
scripture.quote: Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age

q: Why did Jesus come back to life?
little: Because God is stronger than death! Jesus rose on Easter morning. That is why we are happy at Easter.
big: Jesus rose because God the Father raised him. It shows that Jesus is who he said he was, and that death is not the end for us either. The Resurrection is the main thing Christians believe. Jesus was not a ghost. He had a real, new, glorified body.
more: Children may ask what it was like. The Church says the Resurrection is a real event, but one beyond our usual experience. It is not like coming back to the same life as before.
avoid: Do not say Jesus "woke up" or "was only sleeping".

scripture.label: Luke 24:6
scripture.quote: He isn’t here, but is risen

q: Why was Jesus born in a stable?
little: There was no room at the inn. Jesus came as a tiny baby in a poor place. God chose to come close to everyone, even the poor.
big: Mary and Joseph were far from home, and there was no room for them in the inn. So Jesus was laid in a feeding trough. God did not come as a rich king. He came as a poor baby, so that nobody feels too small or too poor for him.
more: Details like the exact stable and the ox and donkey come from tradition; the Bible says only "a feeding trough".
avoid: Do not say the innkeeper was mean. The Bible does not say that.

scripture.label: Luke 2:7
scripture.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

little: Yes. Jesus promised to come again. We do not know when, so we try to live well and love people while we wait.
big: Yes. The Creed says Jesus "will come again in glory". Nobody knows the day or hour, not even the angels. Jesus told us to be ready by loving God and our neighbour. We do not need to be scared; we hope.
more: Some children hear predictions about the end of the world on the internet. Gently say the Church does not teach anyone can know the date, and Jesus himself said so.
avoid: Avoid "be good or Jesus will catch you".

scripture.label: Acts 1:11
scripture.quote: who also said, “You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.”

scripture.label: Matthew 24:36
scripture.quote: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

little: Yes. Jesus healed sick people, made the blind see, and calmed storms. These were signs that God’s love is real and strong.
big: Yes. The Gospels tell of Jesus healing, feeding crowds and calming the sea. The Church calls them signs. They show that God’s kingdom is near and that Jesus is who he says he is. But Jesus did not heal everyone, and the Church does not say why.
more: If your child asks "why does God not do miracles now?", you can say that God does still work wonders, and that most of his work is quiet, in love and kindness.
avoid: Do not promise that praying will always heal.

scripture.label: John 2:11
scripture.quote: This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

little: Joseph was Mary’s husband, and he took care of Jesus. He was a carpenter. He was kind, brave and quiet. Jesus obeyed him.
big: Joseph was a carpenter in Nazareth. He was married to Mary and looked after Jesus as a father would. The Church says Joseph was Jesus’ legal or foster father, because Jesus is the Son of God. Joseph is the patron of the whole Church and a model for workers and fathers.
more: A good place to talk about families that are not "traditional": Joseph shows that loving care makes a father.
avoid: Avoid claims about Joseph’s age or death that are not in the Bible.

scripture.label: Luke 2:51
scripture.quote: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.

little: Yes, Jesus loves you very much. He loves you when you are happy and when you are sad. He will never stop.
big: Yes. The Church teaches that Jesus knew and loved each one of us when he gave his life. His love is personal: "He loved me and gave himself for me". That includes you, by name.
more: Say it often. Children need to hear it more than we think.
avoid: Avoid "Jesus loves you, so you must behave". Love comes first.

scripture.label: John 15:9
scripture.quote: Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you

little: We trust that Grandpa is with God. God loves him very much. We miss him, and it is okay to be sad. We can still pray for him and talk to God about him.
big: When someone who loved God dies, we believe they are in God’s care. The Church teaches that those who die in God’s friendship live with him for ever. We also trust God’s mercy for everyone we love. Death hurts because we love; the Church says that love does not end. We can pray for Grandpa, and Mass is offered for those who have died.
more: The Church does not tell us exactly what it is like or where. She invites us to trust in God’s mercy. You can say "I do not know everything, but I know God is good."
avoid: Avoid "he is just sleeping", "God needed another angel", or "he is watching you every minute". Children may be afraid to sleep, or feel God took him.

scripture.label: Wisdom 3:1
scripture.quote: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them.

mystery: The Church does not say exactly what the dead experience. She teaches that we can trust God and pray for them.

little: We know God loves his animals. The Church does not say exactly what happens to them when they die. We can be sure God is good, and we can thank him for our pets.
big: The Church teaches that animals are God’s creatures. God cares for them, and we should be kind to them. But the Church has never defined that animals have an afterlife, and it has not said they do not. So the honest answer is: we do not know, and we trust God’s goodness.
more: Many children ask this when a pet has died. You can allow the sadness and say that love for a pet is a good thing. Some saints and theologians have hoped for animals, but that is hope, not Church teaching.
avoid: Avoid giving a firm "yes" or "no" as if it were Church teaching. Avoid "it is only an animal".

scripture.label: Psalm 121:4
scripture.quote: Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

mystery: The Church has no definition of what happens to animals after death.

little: Heaven is being with God, who loves us. There will be no more crying, and we will be very happy. We do not know all about it, but it will be good.
big: Heaven is a life of joy with God, with Mary and the saints, and with all who love him. The Bible uses pictures such as a feast and a city of light because it is hard to describe. The Church says heaven is beyond all we can imagine. We will be fully ourselves, and fully happy.
more: Do not worry about not having a clear picture. Pictures of clouds and harps are only pictures.
avoid: Avoid picturing heaven as just "floating on clouds".

scripture.label: Revelation 21:4
scripture.quote: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”

mystery: The Church says heaven is beyond what we can describe.

little: When we die, our body stops working. But we do not stop. We believe God takes care of us. At the end of time, God will make everything new.
big: When a person dies, the body stops living and the soul goes to God. The Church teaches that at the end of the world God will raise our bodies too, as he raised Jesus. Dying is sad, but for Christians it is not the end.
more: Children sometimes ask if it hurts. You can say that most people who die are cared for, and that God is with them. Answer honestly and calmly.
avoid: Do not say death is "like sleep". Say the person has died, and their body does not feel anything.

scripture.label: Philippians 1:23
scripture.quote: But I am hard pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better.

little: Your soul is the part of you that loves and knows God. It is the real you inside. God made your soul, and it never dies.
big: The soul is what makes each person alive in a special way. It is spiritual, and God creates it when a person begins. The Church teaches that it does not die when the body does. Each of us is a body and a soul together.
more: Children may ask about animals. See the question about animals: the Church has not defined what happens to them after death.
avoid: Do not say the soul is a ghost that lives inside you.

scripture.label: Genesis 2:7
scripture.quote: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

little: Because the world is not yet the way God wants it to be. Death is sad. But Jesus beat death, and one day God will take it away.
big: The Church teaches that death entered the world because of sin. God did not want us to die. Jesus has shown that death is not the end, and one day God will wipe away every tear. For now, death is a sad thing, and we mourn.
more: Do not worry about explaining Adam and Eve in detail. Just say that sin broke things, and God is mending them.
avoid: Avoid "God took them because they were good" or "it was their time".

scripture.label: Revelation 21:4
scripture.quote: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”

little: Some people who love God still need to get ready to meet him face to face. Purgatory is a time of getting ready, with God’s love. It is not a scary place.
big: The Church teaches that those who die in God’s friendship but are not fully ready are made clean so they can enter heaven. This is called purgatory. They are already saved. That is why we pray for the dead.
more: The Church does not say how long it is or where it is. Pictures of fire are old pictures; the Church mainly teaches purification.
avoid: Do not describe it as a place of punishment like hell.

scripture.label: 2 Maccabees 12:45
scripture.quote: But if he was looking forward to an honorable memorial of gratitude laid up for those who die in godliness, then the thought was holy and godly. Therefore he made the atoning sacrifice for those who had died, that they might be released from their sin.

mystery: The Church does not tell us how purgatory works, only that it is real and that we can pray for those in it.

little: God wants everyone to be with him. Hell is what happens when a person says no to God for ever. God never wants that for anyone.
big: The Church teaches that hell is real. It is being separated from God, because a person freely and finally refuses God’s love. God does not send anyone there. He wants everyone to be saved. The Church does not say that any particular person is in hell.
more: Keep it short with young children. If they are afraid, remind them that God is a loving Father and that nobody ends up in hell by mistake or by one small sin.
avoid: Never use hell as a threat. Avoid "you will go to hell if you do that".

scripture.label: 1 Timothy 2:4
scripture.quote: who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.

mystery: The Church does not say who, if anyone, is in hell.

q: Why do we pray for people who have died?
little: Because we still love them, and love does not stop. We ask God to take good care of them.
big: The Church has prayed for the dead from the earliest days. We believe the dead are still part of God’s family, and our prayers can help them. We pray for them at Mass, on All Souls’ Day, and in our own prayers.
more: This is a lovely thing for a grieving child to do. A short prayer is enough: "Lord, please take care of Grandpa."
avoid: Do not say prayers for the dead are "just in case".

scripture.label: 2 Maccabees 12:45
scripture.quote: But if he was looking forward to an honorable memorial of gratitude laid up for those who die in godliness, then the thought was holy and godly. Therefore he made the atoning sacrifice for those who had died, that they might be released from their sin.

little: No! Heaven is the happiest place there is, because we will be with God, who is love. It will be better than the best day ever.
big: Heaven is not boring, because God is not boring. The Bible says that in God’s presence there is "fullness of joy". Heaven is not a quiet waiting room. It is a life of love, joy and friendship that never ends.
more: This is a great chance to ask what the child loves best and say that heaven will be a fuller version of what is good.
avoid: Do not promise specific things, like "you will have every toy".

scripture.label: Psalm 16:11
scripture.quote: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.

q: When is the end of the world?
little: Nobody knows when, only God the Father. We do not need to be afraid. God is in charge, and he is good.
big: Jesus said no one knows the day or hour, not even the angels. The Church teaches that Jesus will come again, but she does not give dates. We can be ready by loving God and one another every day.
more: If a child has heard a scary prediction, you can say that people have said this for many centuries, and Jesus told us not to worry about guessing.
avoid: Do not repeat date predictions.

scripture.label: Matthew 24:36
scripture.quote: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

q: Why do we have to go to Mass?
little: Mass is where we meet Jesus and our church family. It is Jesus’ special gift to us. Sunday is the Lord’s Day, so we go to say thank you.
big: At Mass we listen to God’s word and receive Jesus in the Eucharist. The Church asks Catholics to go every Sunday because the Eucharist is the heart of our life as Christians. Sometimes it feels long, and that is normal. It is okay to say Mass is hard sometimes.
more: If a child says "God is everywhere, why church?", say that we come together as his family, and that Jesus asked us to. The Church excuses those who cannot go for serious reasons, such as illness.
avoid: Avoid "you have to or God will be angry" and bribing with treats afterwards. Try "this is what our family does, and here is why it matters".

scripture.label: Hebrews 10:25
scripture.quote: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

q: Is it really Jesus in the bread at Mass?
little: Yes. Catholics believe that at Mass the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Jesus. It still looks like bread, but it is Jesus.
big: Jesus said "This is my body". The Church has always believed he meant it. After the priest prays at Mass, the bread and wine become Jesus’ Body and Blood, though they still look and taste the same. This is a mystery we believe because Jesus said so.
more: This is one of the biggest things Catholics believe. Children can take it simply. If they ask "how?", say it is a mystery and a gift.
avoid: Do not say it is "just a symbol". The Church teaches it is more than that.

scripture.label: Luke 22:19
scripture.quote: He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”

scripture.label: John 6:51
scripture.quote: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”

q: Why can’t I have Communion yet?
little: You are getting ready to meet Jesus in a special way. You will learn what Communion is, and then you will receive it. It will be a big day!
big: Catholics receive their first Holy Communion when they are old enough to understand what it is, and they have made their first Confession. Learning about it helps us receive Jesus with love. In the meantime, you can still come to Mass and join in the prayers.
more: Some children ask because they see everyone else going up. A blessing from the priest is often offered. Talk about the date to look forward to.
avoid: Do not say "you are not good enough yet".

scripture.label: Luke 22:19
scripture.quote: He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”

little: Baptism is the sacrament where we become God’s children and members of the Church. Water is poured, and we are welcomed into God’s family.
big: In Baptism, water is poured and the words are said: "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit". This takes away sin, gives new life with God, and makes a person a member of the Church. Babies and grown-ups can both be baptized.
more: Baptism is also a good time to talk about the child’s name and godparents.
avoid: Do not say that unbaptized people are not loved by God.

scripture.label: Matthew 28:19
scripture.quote: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

q: Why do we tell our sins to a priest?
little: Because Jesus gave the Church the gift of forgiveness. In Confession we say sorry, and God forgives us and gives us a fresh start.
big: Jesus told his apostles that they could forgive sins. The priest does this in Jesus’ name. Confession is private: the priest can never tell anyone what he hears. Saying sorry out loud helps us to be honest, and we leave feeling lighter.
more: Many children are nervous about Confession. You can go with them. The priest is kind and has heard it all before.
avoid: Never use Confession as a threat or punishment.

scripture.label: John 20:23
scripture.quote: If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”

scripture.label: 1 John 1:9
scripture.quote: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

q: Why do we make the Sign of the Cross?
little: It is a prayer with our body. We say "Father, Son and Holy Spirit", and we remember that Jesus died on a cross because he loves us.
big: The Sign of the Cross reminds us of Jesus’ cross and of the Trinity. We make it at the start of prayer, at Mass, and at many other times. It is a very old Christian habit, and it is a way of saying "I belong to God".
more: Little ones can learn it as a movement before they understand the words.
avoid: Avoid saying it is a "good luck charm".

scripture.label: Matthew 28:19
scripture.quote: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

q: Why do we have a pope?
little: Jesus chose Peter to lead his friends, and the pope is Peter’s successor. He helps keep the whole Church together.
big: Jesus gave Peter a special job as shepherd of his Church. Catholics believe the pope is Peter’s successor, the bishop of Rome. He serves the unity of the Church. We pray for him every Mass.
more: Other Christians see this differently. It is fair to say that not all Christians agree about the pope, and that we respect them.
avoid: Do not say the pope never makes mistakes about everything. The Church only teaches that in certain solemn teachings about faith and morals.

scripture.label: Matthew 16:18-19
scripture.quote: I also tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.  I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”

little: Over time Christians have disagreed and split apart. But all baptized Christians belong to Jesus. Jesus prayed that we would all be one.
big: In history, Christians disagreed, and some groups separated. The Church says we should not blame people born into those groups. She says many good things are found in other Christian churches too. Jesus prayed that his followers would be one, and Catholics pray and work for that.
more: Children often have friends from other churches. Encourage respect and friendship.
avoid: Avoid putting down other churches or saying they are wrong about everything.

scripture.label: John 17:21
scripture.quote: that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.

q: My friend isn’t Christian. Will they go to heaven?
little: God loves your friend and wants your friend to be with him. We trust God to be fair and kind. We can pray for your friend, and be a good friend.
big: The Church teaches that Jesus is the way to God. She also teaches that people who, through no fault of their own, do not know Jesus, but sincerely seek God and try to do what is right, can be saved. God desires all people to be saved. We leave the judging to God, who is just and merciful.
more: This is a good time to talk about kindness and respect for people of all faiths. The best witness is how we treat our friend.
avoid: Do not say "your friend will go to hell". The Church does not say that.

scripture.label: 1 Timothy 2:4
scripture.quote: who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.

mystery: The Church does not say exactly how God saves people who do not know Christ; she trusts God’s mercy.

q: Why do we stand, sit and kneel at Mass?
little: Our bodies pray too. We stand to listen to the Gospel, sit to listen, and kneel to show how great Jesus is.
big: At Mass we use our whole body to pray. We stand to show respect, sit to listen and think, and kneel to adore Jesus. It also helps us all pray together as one family.
more: Children who fidget can be told it is okay. Joining in the movements helps them focus.
avoid: Do not scold during Mass for small movements. It can turn Mass into a dislike.

scripture.label: Psalm 95:6
scripture.quote: Oh come, let’s worship and bow down. Let’s kneel before the LORD, our Maker,

q: Why do we read the Bible at Mass?
little: Because the Bible is God’s word to us. At Mass God talks to us through the readings, and we listen.
big: The Bible is the word of God written by people with God’s help. At Mass we hear readings from the Old and New Testaments and the Gospel. Hearing it together helps us know God and one another.
more: You can read the Sunday Gospel together before Mass so the child knows what to listen for.
avoid: Do not say the Bible is only for adults or priests.

scripture.label: 2 Timothy 3:16
scripture.quote: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,

q: Why do we give things up in Lent?
little: Lent is a time to get ready for Easter. We give up something small, pray more and help others. This helps us love God more.
big: In Lent, Christians fast, pray and give to the poor. These help us turn our hearts to God. Giving up a treat is a small way to say "God is more important than sweets". The point is love, not showing off.
more: A good family idea is to give up something and give the money or time to someone in need.
avoid: Do not say Lent is about being miserable or earning God’s love.

scripture.label: Matthew 6:17-18
scripture.quote: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,  so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

q: Why do we pray to saints?
little: Saints are people who are with God in heaven. We ask them to pray for us, like asking a friend or grandparent to pray for you. We only worship God.
big: The saints are alive with God, and they love us. When we pray "Saint Anne, pray for us", we are asking a friend in heaven to pray with us. It is like asking a friend on earth to pray for you. We worship only God, never the saints.
more: The Bible says the prayer of a righteous person is powerful. Catholics believe the righteous in heaven are still praying.
avoid: Avoid saying saints "give" us things. They pray for us; God gives.

scripture.label: James 5:16
scripture.quote: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

little: Mary is Jesus’ mother. God chose her, and she said yes. She is also our mother in heaven, who loves us and prays for us.
big: Mary is the mother of Jesus, and so the Church calls her Mother of God, because Jesus is God. She said yes to God’s plan and she was with Jesus even at the cross. Jesus gave her to us as our mother too. The Church honours her, but does not worship her.
more: Children who have lost a mother, or are in a hard situation, can find comfort in knowing Mary is a mother to them.
avoid: Do not say that Mary is equal to God.

scripture.label: Luke 1:42
scripture.quote: She called out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!

q: Why do we pray to Mary?
little: We ask Mary to pray for us, because she is Jesus’ mother and she loves us. The Hail Mary begins with words from the Bible.
big: The Hail Mary starts with the angel’s greeting and Elizabeth’s words from the Gospel of Luke. We ask Mary to pray for us "now and at the hour of our death". She always leads us to Jesus. We do not worship her. We ask her to pray with us.
more: Praying the Rosary with a child can start with one decade. The beads give little hands something to do.
avoid: Avoid saying that we pray to Mary instead of to Jesus.

scripture.label: Luke 1:28
scripture.quote: Having come in, the angel said to her, “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!”

little: No. We worship only God. A statue is like a photo of someone we love. It helps us remember them and pray.
big: No. Catholics worship God alone. Statues and pictures remind us of Jesus, Mary and the saints, as photos of family remind us of them. The Church says that honour given to a picture goes to the person it shows.
more: The first commandment forbids idols. The Church says that honouring holy images is not idolatry, because we are honouring the people, not the objects.
avoid: Do not make fun of people of other faiths about their images.

scripture.label: Exodus 20:3
scripture.quote: “You shall have no other gods before me.

q: What is a saint? Can I be one?
little: A saint is someone who loves God very much and is with him in heaven. Yes, you can be one! God wants all of us to be holy.
big: Saints are people who followed Jesus in a special way and are now with God. The Church names some saints so we can look to them. But everyone is called to be a saint. Most saints were ordinary people who loved God in small things.
more: Children enjoy reading about saints their age. This is a good way to introduce lives of the saints.
avoid: Avoid giving the idea that saints never had problems. Many struggled.

scripture.label: Matthew 5:48
scripture.quote: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.

q: Do I have a guardian angel?
little: The Church teaches that God gives angels to help us. Many people pray to their guardian angel. You can say hello to yours!
big: The Church teaches that angels are real and that they watch over people. A tradition teaches that each person has a guardian angel from the start of life. Jesus said that children’s angels see the face of the Father.
more: The Guardian Angel prayer is a good short bedtime prayer for children.
avoid: Do not say angels are people who died. Angels are a different kind of being.

scripture.label: Matthew 18:10
scripture.quote: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

little: Yes. Angels are real. They are God’s helpers and messengers. They do not have bodies like ours.
big: The Church teaches that angels are real. They are spirit beings who serve and praise God and help people. In the Bible they bring messages, like at Christmas. We cannot see them, but the Bible says they are close.
more: Pictures of angels with wings are symbols. Be careful not to say angels are people who became angels.
avoid: Avoid "when people die they become angels".

scripture.label: Psalm 91:11
scripture.quote: For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

little: The Church teaches that there are bad angels who said no to God. But they are much, much weaker than God. You do not need to be scared. God is with you.
big: The Church teaches that the devil is a fallen angel who turned against God. He is real, but he is only a creature, and his power is not infinite. God is far stronger. You can ask Jesus and your guardian angel for help.
more: Fear of the devil can keep children awake. Keep the focus on Jesus. A simple prayer, like "Jesus, help me", is enough.
avoid: Do not blame the devil for everything, or use him as a threat.

scripture.label: 1 John 4:4
scripture.quote: You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.

little: There was a real man called Saint Nicholas, who loved God and gave gifts to the poor. Santa Claus comes from stories about him.
big: Saint Nicholas was a bishop who lived long ago in what is now Turkey. He was known for helping the poor in secret. Santa Claus is a Christmas story that grew from his name. It is a game of giving. The real heart of Christmas is Jesus’ birth.
more: Families handle this differently. A kind way is to ask the child, "What do you think?" If they truly ask, answer honestly. What matters is that they never feel tricked, and that Christmas stays about Jesus. (St Nicholas facts here are from settled history, not from the Catechism.)
avoid: Do not lie to a child who sincerely asks. Do not use "Santa is watching" to control behaviour.

scripture.label: Matthew 25:35
scripture.quote: for I was hungry and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me drink. I was a stranger and you took me in.

little: We do not know all the reasons. God did not want bad things. He is with us when they happen, and he can bring good even from sad things.
big: This is one of the hardest questions. The Church says there is no quick answer. God made a good world, but it is not yet finished, and people can choose wrong. God never wants evil. He is always with us, and he can bring good out of it. In the end, Jesus will make everything new.
more: It is fine to say "I do not know". Do not offer neat reasons for specific sufferings. Sit with the child.
avoid: Avoid "God had a plan" or "everything happens for a reason" for a particular sad event.

scripture.label: Romans 8:28
scripture.quote: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.

mystery: The Church says the ways of God’s providence are often unknown to us.

little: All living things die one day. It is very sad. It is okay to cry. You loved your pet, and that is a good thing.
big: Pets die because everything in this world has a time. It is not your fault, and it is not a punishment. The Church teaches that animals are God’s creatures and that we should be kind to them. Grieving is a sign of love.
more: A small ceremony, a prayer or a drawing can help. See also: Do animals go to heaven?
avoid: Do not rush to replace the pet. Do not say "it was only an animal".

scripture.label: Psalm 34:18
scripture.quote: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

little: God is with you in the dark, just as in the light. You can say "Jesus, stay with me". Your guardian angel is with you too.
big: The Bible says "I will fear no evil, for you are with me". God does not sleep. You can pray a short prayer, like the Guardian Angel prayer, and ask God to keep you safe. A night-light is fine, too.
more: Children’s fears are real, even if the thing is not. Listen first, and then pray.
avoid: Do not say "do not be silly".

scripture.label: Psalm 23:4
scripture.quote: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.

q: Why do I feel sad sometimes?
little: Everyone feels sad sometimes. It is part of being a person. God is close to you when you are sad, and you can tell him how you feel.
big: Feelings are not good or bad in themselves. Sadness can mean that you miss someone or that something hurt. God is close to the broken-hearted. It helps to tell someone you trust, and to tell God too. If the sadness lasts a long time, tell a grown-up.
more: Take sadness seriously. If it lasts or seems heavy, talk to a doctor or counsellor. Faith and professional care work together.
avoid: Do not say "just pray and you will be fine" or "you should be happy".

scripture.label: Psalm 34:18
scripture.quote: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

little: Sickness is part of living in this world. God does not want us to suffer. Jesus cared for sick people, and he cares for you.
big: Illness is a hard part of life. The Church says Jesus had great compassion for the sick and healed many. He did not heal everyone, and the Church does not explain why. We care for sick people and pray for them, and there is a sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
more: If a child is sick or has a sick loved one, be honest and gentle. Do not promise healing.
avoid: Do not say sickness is a punishment.

scripture.label: Psalm 34:18
scripture.quote: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

little: Because people choose to hurt each other. God wants peace. We can pray for peace and be peacemakers in small ways.
big: War happens when people choose anger and greed over love. The Church teaches that peace is more than no fighting; it is built by justice and love. Jesus said, "Blessed are the peacemakers". We can pray for peace and be kind.
more: News about war can frighten children. Reassure them they are safe, limit news, and pray together for people in danger.
avoid: Do not say a particular side is a "bad" people.

scripture.label: Matthew 5:9
scripture.quote: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

q: What if my mom or dad die?
little: Most parents live a long time. But if that ever happened, God would be with you, and he would send people to love you. God does not forget you.
big: It is natural to worry. Most children have their parents for a long time, but we cannot promise it. We can promise that God will never leave us, and that he works through people who care for us. The Bible says that even if a mother forgot her child, God would not forget.
more: Do not promise "that will never happen". Say you will do all you can to be safe. If the child worries a lot, hold them and listen.
avoid: Avoid dishonest comfort.

scripture.label: Isaiah 49:15
scripture.quote: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!

q: My parents are splitting up. Is it my fault?
little: No. It is never a child’s fault. Your parents still love you. God loves you and is with you.
big: It is not your fault. Grown-ups’ problems are grown-ups’ problems. Both parents still love you. You may feel sad, angry or confused. All of that is okay. God is close to children in hard times, and you can talk to a trusted adult and to God.
more: Say clearly and often that the child is not to blame. Do not speak badly of the other parent in front of the child. Help the child talk with a school counsellor, priest or family member if they need support.
avoid: Avoid putting the child in the middle or asking them to take sides.

scripture.label: Psalm 27:10
scripture.quote: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.

q: I’m worried about something. What can I do?
little: Tell someone you trust, and tell God. You can say a short prayer, like "Jesus, please help me". Worries get smaller when we share them.
big: The Bible says: "In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition ... let your requests be made known to God". That means you can bring every worry to God. And you can talk to a parent or teacher too. We do not carry worries alone.
more: A "worry jar" or a bedtime talk can help children share. Praying together can calm the body, too.
avoid: Do not say "do not worry" without listening first.

scripture.label: Philippians 4:6
scripture.quote: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

q: Is it okay to be angry at God?
little: Yes. God can handle your feelings. You can tell him honestly how you feel. He still loves you.
big: Yes. In the Bible, many people told God they were upset, even in the Psalms. God does not stop loving us when we are angry. Telling him honestly is a kind of prayer, and it keeps us close to him.
more: This is a healthy thing to say to a grieving child. The Psalms give words for anger and sadness.
avoid: Do not say "you should not feel that" or that God will punish anger.

scripture.label: Psalm 13:1
scripture.quote: How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?

q: Does God still love me when I’m naughty?
little: Yes! God always loves you, even when you do something wrong. He does not like the wrong thing, but he never stops loving you.
big: Yes. God’s love does not depend on how good we are. In Jesus’ story of the lost son, the father runs to meet his son who has done wrong. We say sorry because we want to put things right, not because God will stop loving us.
more: Children need to hear this when they have been in trouble. Separate the act from the child: "What you did was wrong. I still love you, and so does God."
avoid: Never say "God is disappointed in you" or "Jesus is sad because you were bad".

scripture.label: Luke 15:20
scripture.quote: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.

q: Why do I do wrong things when I don’t want to?
little: It happens to everyone. It is hard to be good all the time. That is why we ask God to help us and say sorry when we get it wrong.
big: Even Saint Paul said, "The good I want, I do not do". The Church teaches that since the first sin, we find it harder to do the right thing. But God gives us grace to help. When we fail, we can say sorry and try again.
more: Normalise struggle. A child who knows that everyone finds it hard is less likely to hide mistakes.
avoid: Avoid "you know better".

scripture.label: Romans 7:19
scripture.quote: For the good which I desire, I don’t do; but the evil which I don’t desire, that I practice.

little: Sin is choosing to do something we know is wrong, which hurts our love for God and other people. God forgives us when we are sorry.
big: Sin is when we freely choose something we know is wrong. It hurts our friendship with God and with other people. A mistake or an accident is not a sin. The good news is that God always forgives us when we are sorry.
more: Do not worry a child about accidents. Sin needs knowing and choosing. Talk about being sorry and making things right.
avoid: Do not say "everything fun is a sin".

scripture.label: 1 John 1:9
scripture.quote: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

little: Your conscience is the little voice inside that helps you know right from wrong. God put it in your heart.
big: Conscience is how you know what is right or wrong. God put a sense of right and wrong in each heart. We need to listen to it, and to learn from our parents, from the Bible and from the Church so that it is well trained.
more: You can help children listen by asking, "What do you think the right thing is?"
avoid: Do not say "your conscience is always right". It needs to be formed.

scripture.label: Romans 2:15
scripture.quote: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

little: Saying sorry puts things right. It makes the other person feel better, and it makes our hearts feel lighter. God is happy when we say sorry.
big: When we hurt someone, saying sorry helps to heal the hurt. The Church teaches that being sorry is the first step to being forgiven. God forgives those who are truly sorry. It also helps us to stop and to try again.
more: Model saying sorry yourself. Children learn from watching.
avoid: Do not force a child to say sorry without meaning it. Help them think about the other person.

scripture.label: 1 John 1:9
scripture.quote: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

little: Because God shares with us. Sharing makes people happy, and Jesus said it is more blessed to give than to receive.
big: God gave us everything we have, and we show thanks by sharing. Jesus taught us to care for people in need. The Church calls this a work of mercy. It does not mean we can never keep anything; it means we give with kindness.
more: Start with small things: toys, snacks, time. Let children choose some of what to give.
avoid: Do not shame a child who finds it hard.

scripture.label: Acts 20:35
scripture.quote: It is more blessed to give than to receive

q: Why should I tell the truth?
little: God is truth. When we tell the truth, people can trust us. Lying hurts trust. It is brave to tell the truth, even when we are afraid.
big: The Church teaches that we should speak the truth because God is truth and wills the truth. Telling the truth builds trust. If you have made a mistake, telling the truth is the best way to start putting it right.
more: When a child tells you a hard truth, thank them first. If they are punished for honesty, they learn to hide.
avoid: Do not punish more for honesty than for the act itself.

scripture.label: Ephesians 4:25
scripture.quote: Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another.

q: Why do I have to obey my parents?
little: Your parents love you and look after you. Obeying them keeps you safe and helps your family. Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph.
big: The fourth commandment asks children to honour and obey their parents. Parents care for you and teach you how to live well. Even Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph. It also asks parents to treat children with love and respect.
more: A child should never be told to obey something harmful. If a grown-up asks a child to do something that feels wrong or unsafe, the child should say no and tell another trusted adult.
avoid: Do not use "God says so" for house rules. Explain real reasons.

scripture.label: Ephesians 6:1
scripture.quote: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.

q: What if someone is mean to me?
little: Tell a grown-up you trust. You do not have to put up with being hurt. You can also pray for the person, and try to be kind.
big: Jesus taught us to love our enemies and pray for them. That does not mean letting people hurt you. Tell a parent or teacher so they can help. Forgiving does not mean you must stay near someone who hurts you.
more: Be careful here. If a child is being bullied or hurt, act. Forgiveness comes after safety.
avoid: Do not say "just forgive and forget", or "turn the other cheek" as a reason to stay in a bad situation.

scripture.label: Luke 6:27
scripture.quote: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you

little: Prayer is talking to God, who loves you. It is like talking to a good friend. He is always glad to hear you.
big: Prayer is a living friendship with God. We pray to thank him, to say sorry, to ask for help and to praise him. Prayer does not change God’s love, but it changes us. The Bible says to pray without ceasing.
more: Short prayers during the day work well for children: when waking, at meals, at bedtime.
avoid: Do not say prayer is a way to get what we want.

scripture.label: 1 Thessalonians 5:17
scripture.quote: Pray without ceasing.

q: How do I pray? What if I don’t know what to say?
little: Just talk to God like a friend. You can say thank you, sorry or please. You can also say the Our Father or the Hail Mary.
big: There is no wrong way. You can use your own words, or prayers like the Our Father. The Bible says that when we do not know how to pray, the Holy Spirit helps us. Even sitting quietly with God is a prayer.
more: Offer a simple pattern: Thank you, Sorry, Please, Help. Pray with the child so they hear you.
avoid: Do not make prayer feel like a performance.

scripture.label: Romans 8:26
scripture.quote: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.

q: What if I fall asleep when I pray?
little: That is okay! God still hears you. A child who falls asleep praying is in a good place.
big: Falling asleep while praying is very common, even for grown-ups. Distractions happen in prayer too. The Church says to be patient and keep coming back. God gives sleep to those he loves.
more: Bedtime prayer is a lovely habit. Keep it short and calm.
avoid: Do not scold a child for sleeping during prayer.

scripture.label: Psalm 127:2
scripture.quote: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

q: What if a grown-up asks me to keep a secret that feels bad?
little: Tell a grown-up you trust right away: your mom or dad, a teacher, or someone at church. You will not be in trouble. Good secrets are happy surprises. Bad secrets make you feel scared or yucky.
big: A good secret is a surprise that will make someone happy. A secret that makes you feel scared, worried or uncomfortable is not one to keep. Always tell a parent or another trusted adult. No grown-up should ask you to keep a secret from your parents about your body or about being hurt. Jesus welcomed children and cared for them.
more: Make sure your child knows this: they can always tell you anything, and they will not be in trouble. The Church takes the protection of children very seriously. Teach children the names of body parts and that their body belongs to them. If a child tells you something worrying, believe them, stay calm and get help right away.
avoid: Never say "do not tell anyone", and never tell a child they must be polite to an adult who makes them uncomfortable.

scripture.label: Mark 10:14
scripture.quote: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
